sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 29% to about 2%, non-anginal chest pain to about 4% and atypical angina to about 18%; a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 38% at 118 to about 24% at 175 beats per minute; and being a woman lowers it, through this sum alone, from about 29% to about 9% (being a woman also acts through the low-risk profile, below).

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: A flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises the risk to about 87% and a reversible defect on the thallium scan to about 52%; more ST depression on exercise (about 23% at 0 mm to about 52% at 2.8 mm) and older age (about 27% at 42 to about 32% at 66 years) raise it steadily.

Through this sum alone, each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same (from about 29% at 0 to about 98% at 2 vessels), and higher cholesterol raises the risk steadily (from about 18% at 193 mg/dL to about 52% at 308 mg/dL); both also act through the vessels-and-cholesterol gate (below).

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: Some rarer results also count strongly (the model has little data on this, n = 2 to 17): a downsloping ST segment raises the risk to about 55%, an ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG to about 77%, a thallium result coded 4 to about 99%, and a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers it to about 11%.
This part combines sex, fasting blood sugar and chest pain on exercise, and acts on 165 of 242 training patients, nearly all of them without chest pain on exercise.

Through it, being a woman lowers the predicted risk more when exercise does not bring on chest pain: for a typical patient it falls from about 29% to about 1% without chest pain on exercise, against about 33% to about 10% with it.
Fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL works the same way: it falls from about 29% to about 3% without chest pain on exercise, but stays at about 32% to 33% with it.

This part combines the number of vessels coloured, cholesterol, a high-cholesterol step and a second copy of the low-risk profile, not as a simple sum; it acts on 118 of 242 training patients and lowers their predicted risk (for its typical patient from about 3% without it to about 2% with it).

More vessels and higher cholesterol take that lowering away, so through it they raise the risk: cholesterol steadily up to about 258 mg/dL (between 147 and 325 mg/dL for different patients), then no further, for patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less (for a typical such patient from about 15% to about 29%), but for women and patients without chest pain on exercise it rises in stages.
For men, the first vessel coloured adds risk through this part and further vessels add nothing more: in a step, mainly the first vessel, from about 22% to about 29%.

This part adds up resting blood pressure and cholesterol with fixed weights: through it, higher blood pressure raises a typical patient's predicted risk steadily, from about 22% at 110 mm Hg to about 40% at 155 mm Hg, and higher cholesterol lowers it in an uneven way, from about 34% at 193 mg/dL to about 24% at 308 mg/dL.

evidence.text: It acts on 165 of 242 training patients, nearly all of them without chest pain on exercise, and 51 of them had heart disease.

Through it, being a woman takes a typical patient's risk from about 29% to about 1% without chest pain on exercise, against about 33% to about 10% with it; fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL takes it from about 29% to about 3% without chest pain on exercise, but leaves it at about 32% to 33% with it.
Its formula reproduces the part exactly on all 242 training patients.

parts.name: chol_threshold
parts.original_hypothesis: Node 3040 = ReLU(1.052*chol - 0.864): a one-sided cholesterol threshold. Since cholesterol is z-normalised, this turns on only above ~0.82 SD above the mean. This is the sub-unit that lets cholesterol act as a risk factor only above a level rather than linearly - but it sits inside the 534 gate, which the ablation shows contributes nothing on test.
